ana: heads-up — started bring-up for community/orionx-13b (variant we pulled yesterday). fp16 baseline looks fine but after int4 sweep there's a weird quality regression on summarization/QA evals. sample diffs attached. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

ana: quick notes:
- fp16 eval: rouge-L ~ 41.2, ppl ~ 6.8
- int4 (per-channel, symmetric): rouge-L ~ 35.7, ppl ~ 9.1
- inference logs occasionally show a "kvcache token_id shift" warning during longcontext runs

ana: quant command I used:
```
python infra/quantize.py --model=orionx-13b --bits=4 --scheme=per_channel_sym --calib-samples=2000 --out=/tmp/orionx-13b-int4.pt
```

ana: one noisy log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:01Z] WARN kv_cache: tokenid_mismatch expected=2048 got=2049 headmap=8 seq=1023
[2026-03-15T12:03:01Z] WARN rotary: angle_index_wrap detected head=8 offset=1
```

ana: sample tokens look shifted by one for a subset of contexts — outputs degrade after ~1k tokens. attaching sample prompt + outputs in the thread (pasted below).

jamie: can you paste a minimal repro prompt and the two outputs (fp16 vs int4)?

ana: sure, pasted short version: 
PROMPT: "Summarize the following policy memo about caching and token routing in two paragraphs."
FP16: "The memo outlines a caching strategy..."
INT4: "The memo outlines a caching strategy... unexpected token <|0|> appears, causing truncation"

dmitri: hmm. two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer normalization or BOS/EOS index shifted during conversion, 2) rotary/head-dim mapping wrong in our quant runtime causing headwise phase to drift under int4 quant noise.

eva: also check how embeddings/proj ordering was serialized — we had a similar off-by-one once where the embed projection matrix got saved transposed and it only showed under quant noise.

ml-ci-bot: [ci] quant-eval/orionx-13b-int4 completed — summary metrics: rouge-L: 35.7 (delta -5.5), ppl: 9.1 (delta +2.3). Full report: https://ci.internal/runs/4820000000-orionx-int4

jamie: thanks. @dmitri can you run the tokenizer id-sanity script on the converted checkpoint (quick check)?

dmitri: running now, pasting results: 
```
# ckpt-inspect tokenizer-index-check /tmp/orionx-13b-int4.pt
found_vocab_size: 50256
max_token_id_in_weights: 50255
bos_index: 1
eos_index: 2
offset_map: none
no obvious out-of-range ids
```

dmitri: tokenizer seems fine. next I'll dump rotary params and compare head offsets vs fp16.

ana: for reproducibility I also tried int4 with asym-per-tensor scheme and saw smaller but still present regression (rouge-L 38.0). so scheme matters but doesn't fix it.

eva: that pattern (worse under per-channel symmetric, slightly better under per-tensor asym) screams headwise scaling sensitivity. Could be a lost sign during qparams clamp or a missing bias correction in the quant codepath.

dmitri: dumping rotary angles now... slow but will post diffs. if there's head permutation or an off-by-one head map, the kvcache index warnings would line up.

ml-ci-bot: [ci] artifact uploaded: /artifacts/orionx-rotary-dump-4820000000.tar.gz

jamie: action items:
- dmitri: compare rotary tensors (fp16 vs int4) and check per-head mean/var, sign flips, and head permutation
- ana: add a minimal repro script that runs longcontext >1k tokens to reproduce kvcache warn reliably
- eva: try a constrained quant (freeze rotary params to fp16 during quant) to see if it's the immediate culprit

ana: noted, I can add repro and run eva's frozen-rotary test tonight.

dmitri: preliminary diff: one head (head 8) shows a small constant offset ~+0.003 in int4 dequantized rotary cos table compared to fp16; looks like low-bit rounding bias. not a permutation but a bias in the scale/zero_point calculation for that shard.

eva: if it's a rounding bias localized to a shard, we can try per-shard zero-point recalibration (calib on more samples) or fall back to fp16 for rotary tables only. both are easy to toggle in the runtime.

ana: thanks. that matches the log head=8. i'll run frozen-rotary + recalib tonight and post results. 

jamie: great. if frozen-rotary fixes >90% of regression we ship a short-term fix: keep rotary fp16 in int4 model builds and open a bug for quantizer calibration discrepancy. :+1:

ml-ci-bot: [note] linked issue created: internal/ML/quant/4820000000 - "orionx-int4 rotary shard bias"

ana: filing repro and results now. will update thread when I have numbers. thanks all. :pray:
